facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base for EverCommerce Inc. is a software group with one funded debt instrument, a secured term loan of 523.9 US$m at June 30, 2026 maturing in July 2031, and an undrawn revolver. On company Adjusted EBITDA the group is at 2.98x gross and 2.22x net leverage on an LTM basis, down from 3.24x and 2.41x at FY2024, with LTM cash interest cover of 5.31x. The evidence behind this is the filed statements and the company's own Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, and the credit mechanics are favourable: floating-rate exposure is largely fixed by interest rate swaps to October 2027, scheduled amortization is 5.500 US$m per year, and the revolver covenant only springs if revolver borrowings exceed 35% of commitments. The strongest contrary evidence is earnings quality and direction: H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell against H1 2025, add-backs are large and recurring, free cash flow conversion has weakened from 57.3% to 40.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, net revenue retention fell, buybacks consume more than free cash flow, and management says full-year results will trend to the low end of guidance. Limitations carried from the readiness review remain: no credit agreement, no letters of credit amount and no covenant-basis EBITDA. These restrict covenant headroom and net revolver availability, not the reported-fact summary.

facts.label: Debt structure and claims outside debt
facts.text: - Instrument. One term loan: principal 523,875 thousand at June 30, 2026, Term SOFR plus 2.25% with a 0.50% floor, 5.89392% at June 30, 2026, quarterly amortization of 0.25% of original principal, balloon July 2031; revolver capacity 155,000 thousand until July 6, 2026, then 125,000 thousand to July 29, 2030, undrawn (10-Q June 2026 page:18 to page:20). Borrower, co-issuers: not stated in the located text; EverCommerce Intermediate Inc. and various subsidiaries guarantee, and the facilities are secured by liens on substantially all assets including equity of EverCommerce Solutions Inc. (page:51). The revolver covenant is expressed as a first lien leverage ratio (page:52), but the sources do not state the lien ranking of the term loan in those words. No bonds, no indenture, no second-lien debt appear in the sources. - Hedging. Three swaps with 425,000 thousand notional fixing the floating component through October 31, 2027 at 4.212%, 3.951% and 3.395% (page:21). Net swap fair value at June 30, 2026 is an asset of 970 thousand and a liability of 623 thousand (page:25). Fair value of the term loan is about 502.3 US$m against 523.875 US$m principal (page:20), a Level 2 measure from trading prices. - Outside the debt figure. Operating lease liabilities 12,007 thousand (page:18); non-cancelable purchase obligations 31,968 thousand (page:26); contingent consideration for ZyraTalk of up to 6.5 US$m over three years tied to post-combination employment services, current accrual not separately printed (page:12, page:8); sales and use tax provision 7.8 US$m (page:28); customer deposits of 13,051 thousand that customers may reclaim pro rata (page:6, page:15). There are no finance leases (10-K page:169), and a search of the 10-K and the June 2026 10-Q found no pension, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance disclosure. - Litigation. A putative class action in Delaware Chancery (Case No. 2024-0077) challenges the sponsor stockholders' veto over hiring or firing the chief executive; no loss is accrued as not probable and not estimable, oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026, a date before the cutoff whose outcome is not in the sources (page:27). - Covenant. Maintenance-type test applies only to the revolver: if revolving loans excluding letters of credit exceed 35% of commitments at a quarter end, first lien leverage must be 7.50x or less (page:51, page:52). The company reports compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026 (page:54). No reported covenant ratio is printed.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: EverCommerce Inc. is a US-listed, sponsor-controlled provider of vertically tailored software-as-a-service to service-based small businesses in home, health and wellness services, with recurring and re-occurring revenue near all of the total and a large, granular customer base. The evidence runs from the 10-K business description and the revenue model through sponsor control rights to the credit facilities: a business that is diversified and cash generative but dependent on third-party payment processors, with a founder-chief executive and two financial sponsors who can block a change of control, a chief executive replacement or large asset deals. For creditors the mechanics are favourable on diversification and the absence of any documented debt-funded distribution, with the term loan repriced and extended rather than increased. The strongest contrary evidence is that sponsors control board composition and consent rights, share repurchases have been running above free cash flow on an LTM basis, a pending Delaware case attacks the sponsors' veto over the chief executive, and the August 2026 release signals a chief executive change without a date. No transaction in the sources raises new debt. The limits are the absent credit agreement and the absence of any sponsor-level history before the sources start.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No new debt issue appears in the sources for the period under review. The credit facilities were repriced and extended rather than upsized: a December 13, 2024 amendment cut the term loan margin and removed the credit spread adjustment, a June 10, 2025 amendment reduced revolver commitments from 190.0 to 155.0 US$m and extended 125.0 US$m of them, and a July 29, 2025 amendment refinanced the term loan at par, extended its maturity to July 6, 2031 and cut the margin by 25 basis points (10-K page:147, page:148; 10-Q June 2026 page:19, page:20). On July 6, 2026 the remaining 30.0 US$m of the original revolver tranche expired, which is after the quarter end and before the cutoff (10-Q June 2026 page:52). Portfolio changes in the period were the sale of Fitness Solutions to Jonas Software, signed March 13, 2024 with the UK part closing July 1, 2024; the acquisition of ZyraTalk on September 15, 2025 for approximately 36.0 US$m in cash plus up to 6.5 US$m of contingent consideration tied to post-combination employment services; and the sale of the marketing technology business to Ignite Visibility on October 31, 2025 for approximately 45.0 US$m in cash subject to closing adjustments, which became discontinued operations and was followed by a transition services agreement that ran to April 30, 2026 (10-K page:9, page:10; 10-Q June 2026 page:12 to page:14). The sources give no use-of-proceeds statement for the marketing technology sale; the cash flow statement shows net disposal proceeds of 37,051 thousand in FY2025 (EX-99.1 March 2026 page:10), and any link to buybacks is not stated. A search of the 10-K, the two 2026 10-Qs and the 2026 releases for merger, take-private, tender offer and secondary offering found no such transaction. The Delaware case challenging the sponsors' chief executive approval right is the only pending matter bearing on control. The terms and parties of any further sponsor transaction are Not supplied.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: about 97% recurring or re-occurring revenue and a customer base of more than 745,000 with very small average revenue (10-K page:9; 10-Q June 2026 page:33). Mechanic: granularity and subscription terms (contracts with 30-day termination rights exist, per the remaining performance obligations note at 10-Q page:16) mean low concentration but quick churn if small businesses weaken. Implication: revenue is durable in the near term but net revenue retention of about 94% means growth must come from new customers; this counters any assumption of automatic deleveraging through earnings growth. Counter-evidence logged: none conflicting. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: operating costs excluding D&A of 79.8% of H1 revenue against 78.1% and management's stated plan to increase product and sales spending (10-Q June 2026 page:41, page:42, page:44). Mechanic: investment-led cost growth compresses Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow while add-backs remain large (CP-1). Implication: leverage tolerance rests on management's ability to hold the cost base; monitor quarterly margin. - Concentration and dependency. Evidence: payments about 20% of revenue and reliance on Worldpay, PayPal and card networks (10-K page:35, page:38). Mechanic: loss of processor or network access, or a compliance failure, interrupts transaction revenue. Implication: operational single-point exposure that is not visible in leverage metrics. - Sponsor alignment and control. Evidence: sponsor consent rights and approximately 85.7% ownership (10-K page:95); no dividend and cash buybacks. Mechanic: the sponsors can steer capital allocation and block a sale or insolvency filing, while the company's own repurchases raise the sponsors' percentage ownership as shares are retired if the sponsors do not sell, an analyst inference. Implication: creditors rely on the covenant package, which is not supplied; governance quality is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions. - Key uncertainties. The outcome of the Delaware case, the identity and timing of the chief executive transition, covenant capacity for restricted payments and debt incurrence, and the effect of the unremediated material weakness on reported revenue.

- Concentration and dependency. Evidence: payments about 20% of revenue and reliance on Worldpay, PayPal and card networks (10-K page:35, page:38). Mechanic: loss of processor or network access, or a compliance failure, interrupts transaction revenue. Implication: operational single-point exposure that is not visible in leverage metrics.

- Sponsor alignment and control. Evidence: sponsor consent rights and approximately 85.7% ownership (10-K page:95); no dividend and cash buybacks. Mechanic: the sponsors can steer capital allocation and block a sale or insolvency filing, while the company's own repurchases raise the sponsors' percentage ownership as shares are retired if the sponsors do not sell, an analyst inference. Implication: creditors rely on the covenant package, which is not supplied; governance quality is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions.

- Key uncertainties. The outcome of the Delaware case, the identity and timing of the chief executive transition, covenant capacity for restricted payments and debt incurrence, and the effect of the unremediated material weakness on reported revenue.

rows.label: EverCommerce is a sponsor-controlled vertical software group selling to small service businesses, with recurring revenue, a single secured term loan and no new debt issued. Control sits with two sponsors, and a chief executive transition is signalled but undated.
Providence Strategic Growth and Silver Lake parties hold approximately 85.7% of the common stock and hold consent rights over change of control, large asset deals and chief executive changes.
The company has disposed of two businesses and bought one since 2024, and funds share buybacks from cash, with the term loan only repriced and extended.
The business is highly diversified by customer, with approximately 93% of customers each contributing under $2 thousand of revenue, and payments are about 20% of revenue.
A Delaware class action challenges the sponsors' chief executive approval right, with oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026, and its outcome is not in the sources.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: The fundamental credit view for EverCommerce Inc. is stable on current metrics with a negative earnings bias, at a confidence of Medium. Evidence from the financial base shows a single secured term loan of 523.875 US$m maturing in July 2031, an undrawn revolver of 155.0 US$m at quarter end, LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 175.819 US$m, LTM leverage of 2.98x gross and 2.22x net and cash interest cover of 5.31x; the business handoff shows a diversified base of more than 745,000 small service customers with recurring revenue near all of the total. The mechanics supporting the view are low customer concentration, modest amortization, a maturity profile with no principal due before 2030 beyond amortization, and cash on hand that exceeds a year of mandatory debt service by a wide margin. The mechanics pulling against it are a net revenue retention of about 94% for the June 2026 quarter, H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA below H1 2025, investment-led cost growth, a management signal that 2026 will land at the low end of guidance, add-backs of 29.7% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA and an unremediated material weakness in revenue accounting. Credit implication: default risk over the next twelve months is low on these inputs because debt service and amortization are covered several times by operating cash flow and liquidity; leverage tolerance is the issue, because earnings are flat to down while shareholders receive cash through buybacks that exceeded free cash flow over the last twelve months, under sponsor control whose limits in the credit agreement are not visible. The view is bounded by the absent credit agreement, the unreported letters of credit and covenant EBITDA, and the cutoff of the sources at August 5, 2026.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding a committee must read is that the debt structure is simple and conservative on its face: one term loan of 523.875 US$m, secured and guaranteed, repriced and extended in 2024 and 2025, with 425,000 thousand of swaps fixing about 81.1% of the balance until October 31, 2027 and no principal wall before the 2030 revolver and 2031 term loan maturities. Gross leverage of 2.98x and net leverage of 2.22x on LTM company Adjusted EBITDA are below FY2024's 3.24x and 2.41x, and cash interest cover rose from 3.61x to 5.31x. Evidence of mechanism: lower base rates and margin cuts reduced cash interest, and scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m a year is small against free cash flow, so debt service is covered. Implication: near-term payment risk is low.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The second finding is that the headline overstates the earnings base. Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock compensation, amortization of contract costs and non-recurring costs of 52.275 US$m on an LTM basis, 29.7% of the total, and non-recurring costs have been positive in every period shown. Without the stock compensation add-back leverage is 3.47x gross and 2.58x net. H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 85.211 US$m is below H1 2025's 89.902 US$m, LTM is below FY2025, and free cash flow fell from 57.3% to 40.8% of Adjusted EBITDA between FY2024 and LTM. Implication: the leverage cushion is real but narrower than the headline implies, and a continuing earnings decline would move leverage toward the 3.7x area under a 20% stress.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third finding is the guidance arithmetic. Management said on August 5, 2026 that results are expected toward the lower end of the 183 to 191 US$m Adjusted EBITDA range, yet reaching even the low end after the third quarter range of 44 to 46 US$m requires a fourth quarter of 51.789 to 53.789 US$m against 44.155 US$m a year earlier. Implication: either the fourth quarter steps up materially or full-year results land below the stated range; creditors should expect LTM Adjusted EBITDA near the first-half run rate absent evidence to the contrary, which is a monitoring position and not a forecast.

facts.text: The fourth finding is capital allocation and control. Providence Strategic Growth and Silver Lake parties hold approximately 85.7% of the common stock with consent rights over change of control, asset deals above 500.0 US$m, equity issuance to non-strategic financial investors and chief executive changes. The company returned 85.141 US$m through buybacks in FY2025 and 82.105 US$m on an LTM basis against LTM free cash flow of 71.687 US$m. No dividend or debt-funded distribution is documented. Implication: willingness to return cash is demonstrated; capacity to do more depends on credit agreement baskets that are not supplied, so restricted-payment headroom is a priority diligence item.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Business durability: the customer base is granular, with approximately 93% of customers each contributing under $2 thousand of revenue, recurring or re-occurring revenue near all of the total, so no single-customer concentration is indicated; the mechanic is low idiosyncratic loss risk, and the implication is stable revenue visibility in the near term (Documentary Fact in the business handoff). Liquidity and maturity profile: cash of 133.5 US$m, an undrawn revolver of 125.0 US$m after July 6, 2026, scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m a year and no maturity of principal beyond amortization until the revolver in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031 mean refinancing risk is distant, about 56 months to the term loan maturity from the cutoff (Documentary Fact and calculation). Interest rate protection: swaps fixing 425,000 thousand of notional until October 31, 2027 reduce earnings volatility from base rates, and cover of 5.31x is above FY2025's 5.06x (Documentary Fact). Cash generation: operating cash flow after interest covered capital spending, capitalized software and amortization, with LTM free cash flow of 71.687 US$m (Documentary Fact).

Liquidity and maturity profile: cash of 133.5 US$m, an undrawn revolver of 125.0 US$m after July 6, 2026, scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m a year and no maturity of principal beyond amortization until the revolver in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031 mean refinancing risk is distant, about 56 months to the term loan maturity from the cutoff (Documentary Fact and calculation). Interest rate protection: swaps fixing 425,000 thousand of notional until October 31, 2027 reduce earnings volatility from base rates, and cover of 5.31x is above FY2025's 5.06x (Documentary Fact). Cash generation: operating cash flow after interest covered capital spending, capitalized software and amortization, with LTM free cash flow of 71.687 US$m (Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings momentum and quality: Adjusted EBITDA is lower year on year in H1 2026, add-backs are large and recurring, net revenue retention fell to about 94% from about 97%, and the company-defined measure is the only EBITDA available (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Sponsor control and shareholder returns: the sponsors can block a sale or an insolvency filing and approve the chief executive, buybacks have exceeded free cash flow over twelve months, and covenant restrictions are unseen (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Controls and disclosure: an unremediated material weakness in order-to-cash revenue accounting and disclosure controls that were not effective at June 30, 2026 reduce confidence in reported revenue timing (Documentary Fact). Dependency: payments are about 20% of revenue and rely on card networks, Worldpay and PayPal, a single-point exposure not captured in leverage (Documentary Fact). Information limits: no credit agreement, no letters of credit amount, no covenant-basis EBITDA and no filing after August 5, 2026 (Insufficient Information; missing evidence is not treated as adverse).

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports a credit snapshot for the consolidated EverCommerce Inc. group as of the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with bounded limitations: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for every requested consumer. Evidence runs from filed financial reports and earnings releases, through the debt note and liquidity discussion, to the downstream modules. The next evidence action is to obtain the credit agreement and its amendments, plus the amount of letters of credit issued under the revolver, if a covenant or availability test is needed. Source sufficiency is not completion of downstream analysis.

- Financial reports. The 10-K and three 10-Qs are filed, SEC-form reports for the consolidated entity EverCommerce Inc. and subsidiaries, US GAAP, USD in thousands. Continuing operations exclude the marketing technology business sold on October 31, 2025, which is shown as discontinued operations (page:9 and page:10 of the latest 10-Q). Prior-period quarterly comparatives are therefore recast, and the cash flow statements include both continuing and discontinued operations through the sale date. Period labels must be kept distinct: quarter, six months, nine months, fiscal year and last twelve months.

- Earnings releases. They carry reported and adjusted figures with reconciliations, quarter and year-to-date columns, pro forma revenue and guidance. They are attributed management claims and do not override the filings. The August 2026 release says full-year results are expected toward the lower end of the guidance ranges (page:3).

- Legal and financing sources. None is supplied. The credit agreement, its June 2025 and July 2025 amendments, the collateral agreement and the guarantee agreement are described only in the notes and discussion (page:19 to page:21, page:51 to page:54 of the latest 10-Q). The financial base for EverCommerce Inc. is a software group with one funded debt instrument, a secured term loan of 523.9 US$m at June 30, 2026 maturing in July 2031, and an undrawn revolver. ### Debt structure and claims outside debt

- Instrument. One term loan: principal 523,875 thousand at June 30, 2026, Term SOFR plus 2.25% with a 0.50% floor, 5.89392% at June 30, 2026, quarterly amortization of 0.25% of original principal, balloon July 2031; revolver capacity 155,000 thousand until July 6, 2026, then 125,000 thousand to July 29, 2030, undrawn (10-Q June 2026 page:18 to page:20). Borrower, co-issuers: not stated in the located text; EverCommerce Intermediate Inc. and various subsidiaries guarantee, and the facilities are secured by liens on substantially all assets including equity of EverCommerce Solutions Inc. (page:51). The revolver covenant is expressed as a first lien leverage ratio (page:52), but the sources do not state the lien ranking of the term loan in those words. No bonds, no indenture, no second-lien debt appear in the sources.

- Hedging. Three swaps with 425,000 thousand notional fixing the floating component through October 31, 2027 at 4.212%, 3.951% and 3.395% (page:21). Net swap fair value at June 30, 2026 is an asset of 970 thousand and a liability of 623 thousand (page:25). Fair value of the term loan is about 502.3 US$m against 523.875 US$m principal (page:20), a Level 2 measure from trading prices.

- Outside the debt figure. Operating lease liabilities 12,007 thousand (page:18); non-cancelable purchase obligations 31,968 thousand (page:26); contingent consideration for ZyraTalk of up to 6.5 US$m over three years tied to post-combination employment services, current accrual not separately printed (page:12, page:8); sales and use tax provision 7.8 US$m (page:28); customer deposits of 13,051 thousand that customers may reclaim pro rata (page:6, page:15). There are no finance leases (10-K page:169), and a search of the 10-K and the June 2026 10-Q found no pension, retiree medical, factoring or supply-chain finance disclosure.

- Litigation. A putative class action in Delaware Chancery (Case No. 2024-0077) challenges the sponsor stockholders' veto over hiring or firing the chief executive; no loss is accrued as not probable and not estimable, oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026, a date before the cutoff whose outcome is not in the sources (page:27).

- Covenant. Maintenance-type test applies only to the revolver: if revolving loans excluding letters of credit exceed 35% of commitments at a quarter end, first lien leverage must be 7.50x or less (page:51, page:52). The company reports compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026 (page:54). No reported covenant ratio is printed.
### Dimensions reviewed

- Leverage. Gross 2.98x and net 2.22x LTM, below FY2024 on both measures; a small rise from 2.92x gross at FY2025 because LTM EBITDA is below FY2025 while debt fell only by 2.75 US$m of scheduled repayment.

- Coverage. Cash interest cover rose from 3.61x in FY2024 to 5.31x LTM because cash interest fell from 45.548 to 33.109 US$m on lower base rates and the margin reductions in 2024 and 2025 (10-K page:142; 10-Q June 2026 page:48). Interest expense before interest income was 16,369 thousand in H1 2026 against 17,713 thousand in H1 2025 (page:29).

- Cash flow quality. Free cash flow after capitalized software was 79,605 thousand in FY2025 and 71,687 thousand LTM, below FY2024's 94,256 thousand, as capitalized software rose; buybacks of 82,105 thousand LTM exceeded LTM free cash flow of 71,687 thousand, and in FY2025 disposal proceeds of 37,051 thousand were largely offset by the ZyraTalk acquisition outflow of 35,773 thousand (EX-99.1 March 2026 page:10).

- Liquidity. See the chart data; the next scheduled use of cash is amortization of 2.75 US$m in the rest of 2026, buybacks (19.2 US$m authorization remaining, program through December 31, 2026, page:54) and purchase obligations of 7,805 thousand in the rest of 2026 (page:26).

- Data quality. A material weakness in order-to-cash revenue accounting identified at December 31, 2023 was not remediated at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:67) and disclosure controls were not effective at June 30, 2026 (10-Q June 2026 page:56).

- Definition risks. Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock compensation, other amortization of contract acquisition costs and a broad class of transaction-related and non-recurring costs including system implementation, severance and integration (page:39). Add-backs were 52,275 thousand LTM, 29.7% of Adjusted EBITDA.
### Subsequent events and guidance
- July 6, 2026: 30.0 US$m of revolver commitments expired (10-Q June 2026 page:20, page:52).

- August 5, 2026: management said second-quarter results met the revenue guidance midpoint and exceeded the top of the Adjusted EBITDA range, that the outlook for the balance of 2026 has moderated, and that full-year results are expected toward the lower end of the ranges; guidance is revenue 612 to 632 US$m and Adjusted EBITDA 183 to 191 US$m, with third quarter revenue 151.5 to 154.5 US$m and Adjusted EBITDA 44 to 46 US$m (EX-99.1 August 2026 page:2, page:3). The release also refers to Alex as chief executive as the company begins its next chapter; no surname or date is printed in the located text.
- Nothing dated after August 5, 2026 is in the sources, so third quarter 2026 results, if released before the cutoff, are not available here.
## Calculations
All inputs in US$ thousands unless stated; LTM = FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025.
| Item | Formula | Result |
| LTM subscription and transaction fees | 566,915 + 289,449 - 280,620 | 575,744 |
| LTM net income from continuing operations | 18,204 + 16,887 - 6,695 | 28,396 |
| LTM stock-based compensation | 27,929 + 11,650 - 14,827 | 24,752 |
| LTM transaction-related and non-recurring costs | 19,837 + 9,675 - 8,688 | 20,824 |
| LTM other amortization | 6,266 + 3,456 - 3,023 | 6,699 |
| Add-backs LTM | 24,752 + 20,824 + 6,699 | 52,275 (29.7% of 175,819; non-recurring costs alone 11.8%) |
| Sensitivity: leverage without stock compensation add-back | 523,875 / (175,819 - 24,752 = 151,067); net 390,379 / 151,067 | 3.47x; 2.58x |
| Principal debt to carrying value | 523,875 - 2,219 - 714 | 520,942 |
| Share of term loan hedged | 425,000 / 523,875 | 81.1%; weighted swap fixed rate (200 x 4.212 + 100 x 3.951 + 125 x 3.395) / 425 = 3.91% before the 2.25% margin |
| Revolver springing test trigger | 35% x 155,000; 35% x 125,000 | 54,250; 43,750 of revolver loans |
| Proxy first lien leverage vs test | 2.98x proxy against a 7.50x limit, headroom 4.52x | Proxy only: all debt is term loan, EBITDA basis is company Adjusted EBITDA, not covenant EBITDA |
| Guidance arithmetic, low end | Implied fourth quarter Adjusted EBITDA = 183,000 - 85,211 - (44,000 to 46,000) | 51,789 to 53,789 against 44,155 in Q4 2025 |
| Guidance arithmetic, revenue low end | 612,000 - 299,482 - (151,500 to 154,500) | 158,018 to 161,018 against 151,153 in Q4 2025 |

Reading of the guidance rows: the low end of full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance combined with the third quarter range implies a fourth quarter well above both the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first-half run rate. This is arithmetic on the issuer's ranges, not a forecast, and it indicates that the low end is not safely reached on the current run rate unless the fourth quarter steps up.
## Gaps
- Credit agreement, definitions of covenant EBITDA, first lien leverage ratio as computed by the company and the named borrower: Not supplied. Covenant headroom is a proxy only.

- Letters of credit issued against the 20.0 US$m sub-limit: Not supplied after searching all seven sources for letters of credit, LC, standby and undrawn. Undrawn committed facilities are therefore stated gross, not net of letters of credit.
- Cash paid for interest is consolidated and may include swap settlements and amounts for the discontinued business before October 31, 2025; the sources do not split it.

- Net revenue retention was about 94% in Q2 2026 against about 97% in Q2 2025 (10-Q June 2026 page:33); no customer count trend is in the sources beyond more than 745,000 customers at December 31, 2025.
- Q1 2026 and Q3 2025 reports were used only for discrete-quarter Adjusted EBITDA; their balance sheets were not used.
- June 30, 2025 balance sheet and debt are not in the pack, so H1 2025 point-in-time debt rows are Not supplied.
- Third quarter 2026 results and the outcome of the October 19, 2026 hearing: not in the sources.
- The accrual for ZyraTalk contingent consideration is not separately printed.
## Next module

CP-1A should use the financial base above: single secured term loan, undrawn revolver stepping down on July 6, 2026, sponsor control of about 85.7% of the common stock per the 10-K (page:95), the chief executive transition, and the Delaware sponsor-veto litigation. CP-2 should carry forward leverage of 2.98x gross and 2.22x net, the 3.47x sensitivity without the stock compensation add-back, the unremediated material weakness and the guidance arithmetic. CP-5 should check the corrected CP-0 locator, the LTM construction and the proxy status of every covenant statement.

It adds one point not in CP-1: the 10-Q for June 30, 2026 is signed on August 5, 2026 by Eric Remer as Chief Executive Officer (page:59) while the release of the same date refers to "Alex as CEO"; the timing of any transition is therefore not established by the sources.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| EverCommerce is a sponsor-controlled vertical software group selling to small service businesses, with recurring revenue, a single secured term loan and no new debt issued. Control sits with two sponsors, and a chief executive transition is signalled but undated. | Medium | The credit agreement is not supplied, so sponsor consent rights cannot be tested against debt documents, and no dated transition filing is in the sources. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Providence Strategic Growth and Silver Lake parties hold approximately 85.7% of the common stock and hold consent rights over change of control, large asset deals and chief executive changes. | Sponsor control can direct strategy and capital allocation; creditors depend on covenants not seen here for protection. | High |

| The company has disposed of two businesses and bought one since 2024, and funds share buybacks from cash, with the term loan only repriced and extended. | No debt-funded distribution is documented, but buybacks absorb cash that could repay debt. | Medium |

| The business is highly diversified by customer, with approximately 93% of customers each contributing under $2 thousand of revenue, and payments are about 20% of revenue. | Concentration risk is low, while payment-processor dependence and net revenue retention of about 94% for the June 2026 quarter are the pressure points. | Medium |

| A Delaware class action challenges the sponsors' chief executive approval right, with oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026, and its outcome is not in the sources. | An adverse ruling could change the sponsors' governance rights, with effect on control and change-of-control dynamics. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

EverCommerce Inc. is a US-listed, sponsor-controlled provider of vertically tailored software-as-a-service to service-based small businesses in home, health and wellness services, with recurring and re-occurring revenue near all of the total and a large, granular customer base. The evidence runs from the 10-K business description and the revenue model through sponsor control rights to the credit facilities: a business that is diversified and cash generative but dependent on third-party payment processors, with a founder-chief executive and two financial sponsors who can block a change of control, a chief executive replacement or large asset deals. For creditors the mechanics are favourable on diversification and the absence of any documented debt-funded distribution, with the term loan repriced and extended rather than increased. The strongest contrary evidence is that sponsors control board composition and consent rights, share repurchases have been running above free cash flow on an LTM basis, a pending Delaware case attacks the sponsors' veto over the chief executive, and the August 2026 release signals a chief executive change without a date. No transaction in the sources raises new debt. The limits are the absent credit agreement and the absence of any sponsor-level history before the sources start.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence quality | Locator | Credit mechanic and limitation |

| Core activities | Vertically tailored SaaS for service small and medium businesses: EverPro (Home Services), EverHealth (Health Services), EverWell (Wellness Services); Business Management Software is typically the first product adopted | Documentary Fact | High | 10-K page:9, page:11 | Land-and-expand supports retention and cross-sell; vertical software tends to be sticky, an interpretation not a sourced claim |

| Customers | More than 745,000 customers at December 31, 2025, about 68% US-based and 32% international; about 93% contribute under $2 thousand of revenue and about 3% over $5 thousand | Documentary Fact (customer revenue split is a company estimate) | High; estimate qualified | 10-K page:9, page:21 | Very low single-customer concentration limits idiosyncratic loss; small customers are cyclical and churn-prone |

| Revenue model | Subscription and transaction fees (SaaS, payment processing, group purchasing rebates) and Other (services, hardware); about 97% of H1 2026 revenue recurring or re-occurring | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:33 | Revenue visibility is high but transaction and rebate lines respond to consumer spending |

| Payments exposure | Payment-related transactions about 20% of 2025 revenue; dependence on Visa, MasterCard, Worldpay and PayPal | Documentary Fact | High | 10-K page:35, page:38 | Processor or network termination risk is a single-point dependency for that revenue |

| Retention | Annualized net revenue retention about 94% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 against about 97% a year earlier, and about 96% for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:33; 10-K page:120 | Retention below 100% means existing customers contract in aggregate before new customers are added; consistent with the soft growth in CP-1 |

| Growth | H1 2026 revenue growth of 3.2% reported and 2.5% pro forma; Q2 growth of 2.7% and 2.0% | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:38 | Low-single-digit growth limits deleveraging through earnings growth |

| Cost structure | Operating costs excluding D&A are 79.8% of revenue in H1 2026 against 78.1%, driven by sales and marketing and product development investment | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:44 | Margin pressure from discretionary investment is reversible but management states it expects further increases in product development and sales and marketing |

| Capital spending | Purchases of property and equipment plus capitalized software of 17,064 thousand in H1 2026 | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:8 | Capitalized software spend lifts reported earnings relative to cash and reduces free cash flow |

| Working capital | Customer deposits of 13,051 thousand are refundable pro rata; deferred revenue 22,101 thousand | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:6, page:15 | Small but cash-like liabilities that support liquidity optics |

| Workforce | About 1,800 employees across five countries at December 31, 2025 | Documentary Fact | High | 10-K page:23 | Employee expense is the largest cost line in the segment table (page:29 of the June 2026 10-Q) |

| Management view | "While our outlook for the balance of 2026 has moderated and we now expect results toward the lower end of our guidance ranges" | Management Language | Medium | EX-99.1 August 2026 page:2 | Quoted and qualified; consistent with the arithmetic in CP-1 on implied fourth-quarter requirements |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new debt issue appears in the sources for the period under review. The credit facilities were repriced and extended rather than upsized: a December 13, 2024 amendment cut the term loan margin and removed the credit spread adjustment, a June 10, 2025 amendment reduced revolver commitments from 190.0 to 155.0 US$m and extended 125.0 US$m of them, and a July 29, 2025 amendment refinanced the term loan at par, extended its maturity to July 6, 2031 and cut the margin by 25 basis points (10-K page:147, page:148; 10-Q June 2026 page:19, page:20). On July 6, 2026 the remaining 30.0 US$m of the original revolver tranche expired, which is after the quarter end and before the cutoff (10-Q June 2026 page:52). Portfolio changes in the period were the sale of Fitness Solutions to Jonas Software, signed March 13, 2024 with the UK part closing July 1, 2024; the acquisition of ZyraTalk on September 15, 2025 for approximately 36.0 US$m in cash plus up to 6.5 US$m of contingent consideration tied to post-combination employment services; and the sale of the marketing technology business to Ignite Visibility on October 31, 2025 for approximately 45.0 US$m in cash subject to closing adjustments, which became discontinued operations and was followed by a transition services agreement that ran to April 30, 2026 (10-K page:9, page:10; 10-Q June 2026 page:12 to page:14). The sources give no use-of-proceeds statement for the marketing technology sale; the cash flow statement shows net disposal proceeds of 37,051 thousand in FY2025 (EX-99.1 March 2026 page:10), and any link to buybacks is not stated. A search of the 10-K, the two 2026 10-Qs and the 2026 releases for merger, take-private, tender offer and secondary offering found no such transaction. The Delaware case challenging the sponsors' chief executive approval right is the only pending matter bearing on control. The terms and parties of any further sponsor transaction are Not supplied.
### Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour
| Dimension | Documented evidence | Category | Quality | Locator | Mechanic and limitation |

| Control | Sponsor stockholders agreement parties own approximately 85.7% of the common stock; all stockholders agreements parties together approximately 90.1% | Documentary Fact | High | 10-K page:95, page:96 | Two percentages describe different party groups; they are logged, not reconciled |

| Distributions | No dividend paid or planned; credit agreement restricts dividends; cash returned through buybacks of 85,141 thousand in FY2025 and 28,567 thousand in H1 2026 | Documentary Fact | High | 10-K page:110; CP-1 | Willingness: returns go to shareholders as buybacks from cash; no debt-funded distribution or dividend recapitalisation is documented in these sources, and history before 2022 is Not supplied |

| Creditor-adverse conduct | No priming, uptier, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is documented | Insufficient Information | Insufficient | Whole source set | Absence of mention is not evidence of absence; the credit agreement baskets are not supplied, so legal capacity cannot be assessed |

| Litigation | Delaware class action challenging the sponsors' chief executive approval right; oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026 | Documentary Fact | High | 10-Q June 2026 page:27 | Outcome after the August 2026 report is Not supplied |

Overall issuer-level behaviour reading: Neutral or Mixed, as an analyst interpretation. The documented actions are repricing and extension of facilities, scheduled amortization, cash buybacks and no dividend, which are not extraction-oriented on the evidence available. The restraint cannot be tied to covenant protection because the credit agreement is not supplied. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are kept separate: capacity is Not supplied; willingness is shown by buybacks that the company states it expects to fund with existing cash on hand (10-Q June 2026 page:54) rather than new debt; feasibility is supported by undrawn revolver capacity and the liquidity in CP-1.

| October 19, 2026 | Oral argument scheduled in the Delaware case; outcome Not supplied | Scheduled event, date before the cutoff | 10-Q June 2026 page:27 |
### Conflicts and discrepancies logged

- Chief executive identity. The June 30, 2026 10-Q, signed August 5, 2026, names Eric Remer as Chief Executive Officer and Chairman (page:58, page:59), while the release of the same date refers to a new chapter "with Alex as CEO" (EX-99.1 August 2026 page:2). Logged, not reconciled: the sources do not date the transition or name the successor in full.

- Sponsor ownership percentages. 85.7% (sponsor stockholders agreement parties) and 90.1% (all stockholders agreements parties) at 10-K page:95 and page:96 describe different groups; no ownership percentage after December 31, 2025 is in the sources.

- Net revenue retention. The 10-K quotes about 96% for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (page:120) and the 10-Q about 94% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (page:33); different quarters, not a conflict.
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: about 97% recurring or re-occurring revenue and a customer base of more than 745,000 with very small average revenue (10-K page:9; 10-Q June 2026 page:33). Mechanic: granularity and subscription terms (contracts with 30-day termination rights exist, per the remaining performance obligations note at 10-Q page:16) mean low concentration but quick churn if small businesses weaken. Implication: revenue is durable in the near term but net revenue retention of about 94% means growth must come from new customers; this counters any assumption of automatic deleveraging through earnings growth. Counter-evidence logged: none conflicting.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: operating costs excluding D&A of 79.8% of H1 revenue against 78.1% and management's stated plan to increase product and sales spending (10-Q June 2026 page:41, page:42, page:44). Mechanic: investment-led cost growth compresses Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow while add-backs remain large (CP-1). Implication: leverage tolerance rests on management's ability to hold the cost base; monitor quarterly margin.

- Concentration and dependency. Evidence: payments about 20% of revenue and reliance on Worldpay, PayPal and card networks (10-K page:35, page:38). Mechanic: loss of processor or network access, or a compliance failure, interrupts transaction revenue. Implication: operational single-point exposure that is not visible in leverage metrics.

- Sponsor alignment and control. Evidence: sponsor consent rights and approximately 85.7% ownership (10-K page:95); no dividend and cash buybacks. Mechanic: the sponsors can steer capital allocation and block a sale or insolvency filing, while the company's own repurchases raise the sponsors' percentage ownership as shares are retired if the sponsors do not sell, an analyst inference. Implication: creditors rely on the covenant package, which is not supplied; governance quality is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions.

- Key uncertainties. The outcome of the Delaware case, the identity and timing of the chief executive transition, covenant capacity for restricted payments and debt incurrence, and the effect of the unremediated material weakness on reported revenue.
### Monitoring gaps and consumers
| Item | Severity | Why it matters | Action |

| Credit agreement, collateral and guarantee agreements, compliance certificate | Medium | Restricted payments, debt incurrence, lien and asset-sale baskets determine legal capacity for creditor-adverse action | Obtain from the 10-K exhibit index or the issuer |
| Add-back bridge by item for transaction-related and other non-recurring costs | Medium | Large and recurring add-backs affect leverage tolerance | Request the itemised schedule |
| Debt maturity schedule beyond the note table and covenant certificate | Low | Schedule is in the notes; the covenant certificate is not | Obtain certificate |
| Dated disclosure of the chief executive transition | Low | Governance and key-person risk | Search for the Form 8-K or later reports |
| Third quarter 2026 report | Medium | The pack stops at August 5, 2026 | Check filings before the committee date |

Consumer readiness. CP-2 (credit synthesis): ready with limitations; take the control structure, the sponsor consent rights, the behaviour reading of Neutral or Mixed, the retention and payments dependencies and the monitoring gaps; why it matters is that leverage tolerance depends on sponsor behaviour; gap is the absent credit agreement; action is to carry legal capacity as Not supplied. CP-5 (evidence trace validation): ready; take the locators in the tables above and the logged chief executive discrepancy; gap is that the customer revenue split and unit economics are company estimates; action is to check each quote against its page.
## Calculations

None new. No figure is derived in this module. The following figures are taken from the accepted financial base handoff and from filings as printed: LTM gross leverage 2.98x, net leverage 2.22x, cash interest cover 5.31x, add-backs of 29.7% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA, buybacks of 85,141 thousand in FY2025 and 28,567 thousand in H1 2026. Directional statements rest on these printed pairs: net revenue retention about 97% a year earlier against about 94% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026; operating costs excluding D&A of 78.1% rising to 79.8% of revenue.
## Gaps
- Credit agreement and related agreements: Not supplied; sponsor behaviour toward creditors cannot be tested against document baskets.
- Sponsor history before the filings: dividend recapitalisation, prior ownership and earlier financings are Not supplied; the 10-K and 10-Qs searched contain no dividend recapitalisation disclosure.
- Chief executive successor name and date: Not supplied; the release gives a first name only.
- Ownership percentages after December 31, 2025: Not supplied.
- Outcome of the October 19, 2026 hearing and any third quarter 2026 filings: Not supplied.
- Customer revenue split and lifetime value to acquisition cost (10-K page:9, page:11) are company estimates and are used only as Management Language or qualified Documentary Fact.
- Recovery: no recovery conclusion is made; a pledge of substantially all assets and subsidiary guarantees exist, which is a mechanic only.
## Next module

CP-2 should synthesise the credit view using the financial base and this fact pack, with sponsor behaviour carried as Neutral or Mixed, legal capacity as Not supplied, the pending Delaware case and the undated chief executive transition as uncertainties, and the retention and payments dependencies as operating risks. CP-5 should check each locator in the tables and the logged discrepancy about the chief executive.

This handoff synthesizes the fundamental credit view from the accepted source-readiness, financial base and business and transaction handoffs, with direct checks against the filings where a number is re-derived. It makes no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Figures follow the financial base handoff: US$ thousands in the filings, US$m or x in chart tables, LTM meaning FY2025 plus H1 2026 less H1 2025.
## Sources

| CP-0 | 1b69fec6f76b0a3db45b22b03548a19960b48042c9a99336086eb38f6dbef02a | Readiness view READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and its gaps |

Consistency with upstream: no correction is needed beyond the one CP-1 already made to the CP-0 locator. One precision is added here. CP-1 described a proxy first lien leverage of 2.98x against a 7.50x test; that test applies only if revolver borrowings exceed 35% of commitments, and the revolver is undrawn, so the test is not currently operative.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| EverCommerce has moderate leverage of 2.98x gross and 2.22x net, ample liquidity and no term loan maturity before 2031, but flat earnings, large add-backs and sponsor-directed shareholder returns leave the credit view stable with a negative earnings bias. | Medium | Credit agreement and covenant-basis EBITDA are not supplied, and the pack stops at August 5, 2026. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage is 2.98x gross and 2.22x net, and cash interest cover is 5.31x, with most floating-rate exposure fixed by swaps to October 2027. | Debt service is comfortable today; swap expiry in 2027 exposes the whole term loan to base rates. | Medium |

| Cash of 133.5 US$m plus an undrawn revolver of 155.0 US$m at quarter end, falling to 125.0 US$m after July 6, 2026, compares with scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m. | Near-term liquidity risk is low, subject to unknown letters of credit. | Medium |

| LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 175.819 US$m is below FY2025, add-backs are 29.7% of it, and management guides to the low end for 2026. | Leverage is 3.47x gross without the stock compensation add-back, so tolerance is thinner than the headline. | Medium |

| Two sponsors hold approximately 85.7% of the stock with consent rights, and buybacks exceeded free cash flow over the last twelve months. | Cash can leave the group at sponsor-aligned discretion, and covenant limits on this are not visible. | Medium |
### Credit view

The fundamental credit view for EverCommerce Inc. is stable on current metrics with a negative earnings bias, at a confidence of Medium. Evidence from the financial base shows a single secured term loan of 523.875 US$m maturing in July 2031, an undrawn revolver of 155.0 US$m at quarter end, LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 175.819 US$m, LTM leverage of 2.98x gross and 2.22x net and cash interest cover of 5.31x; the business handoff shows a diversified base of more than 745,000 small service customers with recurring revenue near all of the total. The mechanics supporting the view are low customer concentration, modest amortization, a maturity profile with no principal due before 2030 beyond amortization, and cash on hand that exceeds a year of mandatory debt service by a wide margin. The mechanics pulling against it are a net revenue retention of about 94% for the June 2026 quarter, H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA below H1 2025, investment-led cost growth, a management signal that 2026 will land at the low end of guidance, add-backs of 29.7% of LTM Adjusted EBITDA and an unremediated material weakness in revenue accounting. Credit implication: default risk over the next twelve months is low on these inputs because debt service and amortization are covered several times by operating cash flow and liquidity; leverage tolerance is the issue, because earnings are flat to down while shareholders receive cash through buybacks that exceeded free cash flow over the last twelve months, under sponsor control whose limits in the credit agreement are not visible. The view is bounded by the absent credit agreement, the unreported letters of credit and covenant EBITDA, and the cutoff of the sources at August 5, 2026.
### Key findings

The first finding a committee must read is that the debt structure is simple and conservative on its face: one term loan of 523.875 US$m, secured and guaranteed, repriced and extended in 2024 and 2025, with 425,000 thousand of swaps fixing about 81.1% of the balance until October 31, 2027 and no principal wall before the 2030 revolver and 2031 term loan maturities. Gross leverage of 2.98x and net leverage of 2.22x on LTM company Adjusted EBITDA are below FY2024's 3.24x and 2.41x, and cash interest cover rose from 3.61x to 5.31x. Evidence of mechanism: lower base rates and margin cuts reduced cash interest, and scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m a year is small against free cash flow, so debt service is covered. Implication: near-term payment risk is low.

The second finding is that the headline overstates the earnings base. Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock compensation, amortization of contract costs and non-recurring costs of 52.275 US$m on an LTM basis, 29.7% of the total, and non-recurring costs have been positive in every period shown. Without the stock compensation add-back leverage is 3.47x gross and 2.58x net. H1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 85.211 US$m is below H1 2025's 89.902 US$m, LTM is below FY2025, and free cash flow fell from 57.3% to 40.8% of Adjusted EBITDA between FY2024 and LTM. Implication: the leverage cushion is real but narrower than the headline implies, and a continuing earnings decline would move leverage toward the 3.7x area under a 20% stress.

The third finding is the guidance arithmetic. Management said on August 5, 2026 that results are expected toward the lower end of the 183 to 191 US$m Adjusted EBITDA range, yet reaching even the low end after the third quarter range of 44 to 46 US$m requires a fourth quarter of 51.789 to 53.789 US$m against 44.155 US$m a year earlier. Implication: either the fourth quarter steps up materially or full-year results land below the stated range; creditors should expect LTM Adjusted EBITDA near the first-half run rate absent evidence to the contrary, which is a monitoring position and not a forecast.

The fourth finding is capital allocation and control. Providence Strategic Growth and Silver Lake parties hold approximately 85.7% of the common stock with consent rights over change of control, asset deals above 500.0 US$m, equity issuance to non-strategic financial investors and chief executive changes. The company returned 85.141 US$m through buybacks in FY2025 and 82.105 US$m on an LTM basis against LTM free cash flow of 71.687 US$m. No dividend or debt-funded distribution is documented. Implication: willingness to return cash is demonstrated; capacity to do more depends on credit agreement baskets that are not supplied, so restricted-payment headroom is a priority diligence item.

The fifth finding is the set of near-term events: the 30.0 US$m revolver tranche expired on July 6, 2026 leaving 125.0 US$m, a Delaware case challenging the sponsors' chief executive approval right has oral argument scheduled for October 19, 2026 with no outcome in the sources, and a chief executive transition is signalled by the August release without date or full name while the same-day 10-Q is signed by Eric Remer as chief executive. Implication: the pack should be refreshed for third quarter 2026 reporting before a committee relies on it.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Business durability: the customer base is granular, with approximately 93% of customers each contributing under $2 thousand of revenue, recurring or re-occurring revenue near all of the total, so no single-customer concentration is indicated; the mechanic is low idiosyncratic loss risk, and the implication is stable revenue visibility in the near term (Documentary Fact in the business handoff). Liquidity and maturity profile: cash of 133.5 US$m, an undrawn revolver of 125.0 US$m after July 6, 2026, scheduled amortization of 5.500 US$m a year and no maturity of principal beyond amortization until the revolver in July 2030 and the term loan in July 2031 mean refinancing risk is distant, about 56 months to the term loan maturity from the cutoff (Documentary Fact and calculation). Interest rate protection: swaps fixing 425,000 thousand of notional until October 31, 2027 reduce earnings volatility from base rates, and cover of 5.31x is above FY2025's 5.06x (Documentary Fact). Cash generation: operating cash flow after interest covered capital spending, capitalized software and amortization, with LTM free cash flow of 71.687 US$m (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Earnings momentum and quality: Adjusted EBITDA is lower year on year in H1 2026, add-backs are large and recurring, net revenue retention fell to about 94% from about 97%, and the company-defined measure is the only EBITDA available (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Sponsor control and shareholder returns: the sponsors can block a sale or an insolvency filing and approve the chief executive, buybacks have exceeded free cash flow over twelve months, and covenant restrictions are unseen (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Controls and disclosure: an unremediated material weakness in order-to-cash revenue accounting and disclosure controls that were not effective at June 30, 2026 reduce confidence in reported revenue timing (Documentary Fact). Dependency: payments are about 20% of revenue and rely on card networks, Worldpay and PayPal, a single-point exposure not captured in leverage (Documentary Fact). Information limits: no credit agreement, no letters of credit amount, no covenant-basis EBITDA and no filing after August 5, 2026 (Insufficient Information; missing evidence is not treated as adverse).

Thesis. EverCommerce is a diversified, recurring-revenue software credit with moderate leverage, long-dated and modest debt service, and ample liquidity, whose credit quality is held back by flat earnings, large add-backs and sponsor-directed shareholder returns whose limits cannot yet be tested.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Earnings erosion | Net revenue retention below 100%, cost investment ahead of revenue, low-end guidance | Leverage drifts from 2.98x gross toward 3.7x under a 20% EBITDA decline; remains far inside the 7.50x revolver test but reduces tolerance for distributions | Material |

| Earnings quality | Add-backs of 29.7%; unremediated material weakness in revenue accounting | Reported EBITDA and revenue timing may overstate sustainable cash earnings; leverage 3.47x without stock compensation add-back | Material |

| Sponsor-directed cash returns | Buybacks above LTM free cash flow; sponsor consent rights; unseen restricted-payment baskets | Cash and revolver capacity could be used for distributions ahead of debt reduction | Material |

| Rate reset after swaps expire on October 31, 2027 | Floating base rate on the full 523.875 US$m thereafter | Roughly 5.2 US$m more annual interest per 100 basis points on the full balance against about 1.0 US$m now | Minor |
| Payment processor dependence | About 20% of revenue through processors and card networks | Termination or compliance failure interrupts that revenue | Minor |
| Governance events | Delaware case, undated chief executive transition, chief executive share sale plan | Key-person and control uncertainty; no direct debt effect shown | Minor |
| Revolver availability | 30.0 US$m expired July 6, 2026; letters of credit unknown | Net availability could be below 125.0 US$m | Minor |
### Gaps ledger
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Credit agreement, covenant EBITDA definition, restricted-payment and debt baskets, named borrower | Legal capacity for distributions and priming cannot be assessed | Sponsor behaviour, leverage tolerance | Material | Obtain credit agreement and amendments |
| Letters of credit outstanding under the 20.0 US$m sub-limit | Undrawn availability is stated gross | Liquidity | Minor | Obtain from issuer |
| Itemised add-back schedule | Quality of Adjusted EBITDA | Leverage | Material | Request bridge by item |
| Third quarter 2026 results and later events | The pack ends August 5, 2026 | All metrics | Material | Refresh before committee |
| Date and identity of the chief executive transition; Delaware case outcome | Governance and control | Sponsor alignment | Minor | Search later filings |

| Source readiness limits inherited from the first module, including the discontinued-operations recast | Prior-period comparability | Trend statements | Minor | Use continuing-operations bases as in the financial base |
## Calculations
All inputs are from the financial base handoff unless a page is cited. US$ thousands.
| Item | Formula | Result |
| Total debt / Adjusted EBITDA, LTM | 523,875 / 175,819 | 2.98x |
| Net debt / Adjusted EBITDA, LTM | (523,875 - 133,496) / 175,819 | 2.22x |
| Gross leverage without stock compensation add-back | 523,875 / (175,819 - 24,752) | 3.47x |
| Net leverage without stock compensation add-back | 390,379 / 151,067 | 2.58x |

| EBITDA decline needed to reach the revolver test level | 523,875 / 7.50 = 69,850; 1 - 69,850 / 175,819 | 60.3% decline (proxy; covenant EBITDA not supplied and the test is inoperative while the revolver is undrawn) |
| Leverage at the guidance low end | 523,875 / 183,000 | 2.86x |
| Leverage at an annualized H1 2026 run rate | 523,875 / (85,211 x 2 = 170,422) | 3.07x (assumes flat seasonality; H2 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was 90,608 against 89,902 in H1 2025) |
| Free cash flow over scheduled amortization, LTM | 71,687 / 5,500 | 13.0x (free cash flow is after cash interest) |
| Rate sensitivity now (unhedged part) | (523,875 - 425,000) x 1% | 989 per 100 basis points; the 10-K gives approximately 1.0 US$m at December 31, 2025 (page:156) |
| Rate sensitivity after swap expiry | 523,875 x 1% | 5,239 per 100 basis points; cover on LTM cash interest plus that increase 175,819 / (33,109 + 5,239) = 4.58x (mechanical, not a forecast) |
| Liquidity after July 6, 2026 expiry, gross of letters of credit | 133.496 + 125.0 US$m | 258.496 US$m |
| Months from the cutoff to the term loan maturity | November 5, 2026 to July 6, 2031 | About 56 months |
| Guidance arithmetic | 183,000 - 85,211 - (44,000 to 46,000) | Fourth quarter 51,789 to 53,789 against 44,155 |
| Buybacks less free cash flow, LTM | 82,105 - 71,687 | 10,418 |
Checks: leverage figures tie to the financial base handoff; the 60.3% is a proxy and not a covenant headroom; stress cases are mechanical sensitivities.
## Gaps
- Credit agreement and covenant definitions: Not supplied; headroom to any covenant is Not calculable on the covenant basis and only a proxy is shown.
- Letters of credit: Not supplied, so net revolver availability is Not calculable.
- Itemised add-back schedule: Not supplied.
- Third quarter 2026 reporting and the October 19, 2026 hearing outcome: Not supplied; nothing after August 5, 2026 is used as fact.
- No rating, market quote or valuation input is in the context; none is used.
- Recovery: no conclusion is made; security over substantially all assets and subsidiary guarantees are mechanics only.
## Next module

CP-5 should test the evidence trace for the claims above: the LTM Adjusted EBITDA construction, the leverage and cover figures, the add-back share, the guidance arithmetic, the sponsor ownership and consent rights, the buyback and free cash flow comparison, and the proxy status of every covenant statement. Carry forward the limitations on legal capacity, letters of credit and the August 5, 2026 information cutoff.
